text.p: The shareholders of Estonian confectionary producer Kalev on Friday approved the proposals on dividend payments and a bonus share issue.
The company will pay dividends of 22 krooons per share from its 14.8 million kroon net profit in 1996, Tonis Allik, the chairman of the company's board, said.
He added that Kelev planned to stick to the principle of paying dividends to shareholders in the future.
It also approved a bonus share issue of 22 new shares for every existing one to raise its share capital to 78.8 million kroons from 2.5 million kroons.
The aim of the bonus share issue is to make the stock more liquid and to increase its share capital, which has been far too small up to now, Allik added.
